category_title: Students with severe hearing impairment and EAL who use physical gestures and lip-reading to decipher archaic language
minimal_context: The student is participating in a focus group discussion about group work and drama activities.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to start our group work for the drama activity. Please join your assigned group.

STUDENT: (Remains very quiet and does not move toward the assigned group, looking visibly uncomfortable about the group work.)

TUTOR: Go ahead and join them. You need to work together on this.

STUDENT: (Gestures with great earnestness, trying hard to communicate his feelings about joining the group.)

TUTOR: I am not sure what you mean. What are you trying to say?

STUDENT: Nope... No. (. . .) um (.) sometime um there are people that they are don’t take the [cope]... Cope (.) cope... Crope (.) crope (.) crope

options.A: Provide a written or verbal diary with prompts asking how he felt and how to avoid the situation.
options.B: Explain the words or expressions he is trying to use through drawings, translations, or body language.
options.C: Allow the student the freedom to choose his own group for the drama activity.
options.D: Provide a visual 5-point scale chart with numbers, colors, and faces to check in on his anxiety.
